card.name: Apsara Dance
card.era: Imagery from the Angkor period; modern form created 1940s–50s
card.tagline: Cambodia's celestial-nymph dance of curling fingers
card.profile: The Apsara dance (Robam Apsara) is a classical Khmer dance portraying apsaras — celestial nymphs of Hindu and Buddhist legend — known for slow, graceful movements and intricate, hyper-flexible finger and hand gestures, performed in golden costumes and headdresses modeled on the bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat (Royal Ballet of Cambodia, Wikipedia; Aurora Travel). The modern form was created under Queen Sisowath Kossamak in the 1940s–50s, with her granddaughter Princess Norodom Buppha Devi as the first principal Apsara dancer.
card.insight: Apsara dance is the best-known piece of the Royal Ballet of Cambodia, which UNESCO proclaimed a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2003 (inscribed on the Representative List in 2008); the art nearly died under the Khmer Rouge and its revival became a symbol of Cambodian cultural rebirth.

observation.setting: Outdoor ancient stone temple ruins in Cambodia, surrounded by trees and greenery.
observation.dancers: Group of female dancers, initially solo then interacting in small groups of three.
observation.formation_and_space: Dancers appear in doorways, line up horizontally in front of temple structures, and walk along paths in procession.
observation.posture: Torso held upright with a slight backward curve in the lower back, knees slightly bent, weight shifted between feet.
observation.footwork: Precise stepping matching the musical beats, often lifting one foot with bent knees, stepping side-to-side or shifting weight subtly; details obscured by long skirts in some shots.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held in graceful curved shapes with fingers hyperextended backwards, hands making expressive gestures.
observation.hips_and_torso: Subtle hip shifts and gentle torso bends accompanying arm and leg movements.
observation.partnering: None, dancers perform solo choreography simultaneously or in staggered sequences.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Low level transitions including kneeling on one knee or squatting postures; no jumps or fast turns visible.
observation.costume_and_props: Elaborate traditional Cambodian golden headdresses, ornate jewelry (necklaces, armbands, bracelets), tight-fitting golden tops, and patterned traditional wraparound skirts (sampot).
observation.cannot_infer: Precise footwork details are partially obscured by long traditional skirts worn by the dancers.

Three dancers stepping synchronously in a horizontal line with bent knees and expressive hand gestures.
Three dancers holding synchronized arm and hand positions while shifting weight side-to-side in front of temple ruins.
Dancers transitioning from standing to kneeling on one knee on temple steps.
